law: Both PushKit and User Notifications use the Apple Push Notification service (APNs) to deliver push notifications to user devices.
PushKit doesn’t support some special use cases in which access to Apple Push Notification service (APNs) isn’t possible.
If your app provides Voice-over-IP (VoIP) phone services, you may use PushKit to handle incoming calls on user devices.
PushKit provides an efficient way to manage calls that doesn’t require your app to be running to receive calls.
For apps built using the iOS 13 SDK or later, PushKit requires you to use CallKit when handling VoIP calls.
CallKit ensures that apps providing call-related services on a user’s device work seamlessly together on the user’s device, and respect features like Do Not Disturb.
Use CallKit to present these interfaces and manage interactions with them.
If you are unable to support CallKit in your app, you cannot use PushKit to handle push notifications.
If you need to do work in response to an incoming notification—for example, to decrypt content—use a notification service extension to perform that work.
VoIP apps must use CallKit to present the system’s call-related interfaces.
Assign one of your app’s custom objects as a delegate, and use that object to respond to user actions and telephony-related changes.
Your servers handle most of the call-related work required to connect users.

When linking against the iOS 13 SDK or later, your implementation of this method must report notifications of type to the framework by calling the method of your app’s object.
For example, the system reports an error if the user enabled Do Not Disturb.
You must configure your app to handle PushKit-related notifications, and you must supply a server to generate those notifications.
You use your server to generate the push notifications that your app receives.
Apps must have the proper entitlements to receive push notifications.
During configuration, always specify a delegate object to receive notifications.
Assigning a value to the property begins the registration process, so always update that property last.
In order to deliver notifications to a user device, your server must know the address of that device.
To ensure the security of the user’s information, always encrypt the token and all user data before sending it over the network.
Apps receiving VoIP push notifications must report the call quickly to CallKit, so it can alert the user to the presence of the incoming call.
